questions.question:
Select the idiom that gives the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase in the following sentence.

Chanda always annoys everyone by __praising herself__ all the time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Blowing her own trumpet**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase "**praising herself**" refers to someone who talks a lot about their own achievements or good qualities, often to the annoyance of others. (खुद की प्रशंसा करना)

 
 
• **Example**: She always talks about how she was the top of her class and never misses a chance to mention her numerous awards. It's like she's always **praising herself**.
 
 
 
• **Blowing her own trumpet** refers to someone who boasts about themselves or their achievements. (अपनी तारीफ़ खुद करना)
 
 
• **Example**: Rahul never hesitates to remind everyone about his successful project; he's always **blowing his own trumpet**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct idiom is **Blowing her own trumpet**.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crying over spilt milk** refers to wasting time feeling upset about something bad that has happened and cannot be changed. (गतानुगतिक पर पछताना)
 
• **Catching one's eyes** means attracting someone's attention. (किसी की नज़र में आना)
 
• **Facing the music** means to deal with the consequences of one's actions. (परिणाम का सामना करना)

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, "I will see you now".

options.text: He said he will see you now.
He said he will see me now.
He said he would see me then.
He said I will see you now.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**He said he would see me then**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, the tense usually changes.

 
 
• In this case, the **future tense** "**will**" changes to its **past form** "**would**."
 
 
 
• The pronouns also need adjustment according to the speaker's perspective.
 
 
• "**I**" becomes "**he**" and "**you**" becomes "**me**" in the context of the speaker conveying the message to someone else.
 
 
 
• The time expression often changes to reflect the shift in context.
 
 
• "**Now**" changes to "**then**" to signify that the event is being referred to from a point in the past.
 
 
 
• **Direct speech** is usually introduced by a comma and quotation marks, while **indirect speech** does not use quotation marks and the sentence structure changes to make it one continuous statement.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 'He said he would see me then'.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) He said he will see you now**. This option incorrectly retains the future tense "will" and does not adjust the pronouns or time expression for indirect speech.
 
• **Option 2) He said he will see me now**. This option makes the same mistakes as option 1 by keeping "will" and "now," making it unsuitable for indirect speech.
 
• **Option 4) He said I will see you now**. This option does not appropriately change the perspective from first to third person and retains both the future tense and the original time expression, which is not correct for converting to indirect speech.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the italicized word.

"Can I *borrow* your cell?" She asked.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**lend**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The italicised word in the sentence, "**borrow**," refers to taking something from someone with the intention of returning it later (उधार लेना).

 
 
• **Example**: He needed to **borrow **a pen as he had forgotten his at home.
 
 
 
• The correct word, "**lend**," signifies giving something to someone for a short period, expecting it to be returned (उधार देना).
 
 
• **Example**: She decided to **lend **her calculator to her classmate for the exam.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4'**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bite **means to use the teeth to cut into something (काटना).

 
 
• **Example**: The apple was so fresh, he couldn't wait to **bite **into it.
 
 
 
• **Rent **refers to paying someone for the use of (an object, property, or service) (किराया पर लेना).
 
 
• **Example**: They decided to **rent **a car for their vacation.
 
 
 
• **Hire **means to obtain the temporary use of (something) for an agreed payment; it can also mean to employ someone (किराए पर लेना, नौकरी पर रखना).
 
 
• **Example**: She was going to **hire **a dress for the prom night.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The sweater is knitted by Suman.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Suman knits the sweater**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in **passive voice**, indicating that the action (**knitting**) is being done by someone (**Suman**) to something (**the sweater**).
 
• To convert a sentence from **passive **to **active **voice, the **subject **(doer of the action) should be placed **before the verb**, followed by the **object **(receiver of the action).
 
• The correct verb form must be used to match the tense and aspect indicated in the original sentence.
 
 
• In this case, the present simple tense "**knits**" is appropriate, conveying a general or habitual action.
 
 
 
• The structure of an active voice sentence typically follows the format: **Subject + Verb + Object**.
 
• Hence, the correct sentence is '**Suman knits the sweater**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2) Suman be knitted the sweater**. This option is grammatically incorrect and does not correctly convert the sentence to active voice.
 
• **Option 3) Suman have knitting the sweater**. This option misuses the verb form and fails to correctly structure the sentence in active voice.
 
• **Option 4) Suman been knit the sweater**. This option is grammatically incorrect and does not follow the correct format for an active voice sentence.

questions.question:
Choose the option that rectifies the grammatical and spelling errors in the given sentence.

The secret to tightrope walking is to graps the rope between the twos and distribute one's weight evenly on the soles of one's feet.

options.text: to grasp the rope between the toes
evenly on the soul of one's feet
The secrte of tightrope walk is

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**to grasp the rope between the toes**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the original sentence is "**graps the rope between the twos**".
 
• The correct phrasing should be "**to grasp the rope between the toes**".
 
• "**Grasp**" means to seize and hold firmly. (पकड़ना)
 
 
• **Example**: Successful athletes **grasp **the importance of discipline and hard work.
 
 
 
• "**Toes**" refers to any of the five digits at the end of the human foot. (पैर की उंगलियाँ)
 
 
• **Example**: The dancer balanced gracefully on the tips of her **toes**.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct option is **to grasp the rope between the toes**.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 1**".

 

**Correct Sentence**: *The secret to tightrope walking is **to grasp the rope between the toes**__ and distribute one's weight evenly on the soles of one's feet.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **evenly on the soul of one's feet**: This option contains a spelling error; "soul" should be "sole", referring to the bottom part of the foot.
 
• **and distribute ones weight**: This option has a possessive error; it should be "one's weight" to show possession.
 
• **The secrte of tightrope walk is**: This option has a spelling mistake in "secrte" which should be "secret", and a grammatical error, as "tightrope walk" should be "tightrope walking".

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Throw caution to the wind

options.text: To be indecisive or unsure about a decision
To take a big risk or be reckless
To be overly cautious or hesitant
To be too strict or rigid in following rules

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**To take a big risk or be reckless**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Throw caution to the wind**" refers to acting in a way that disregards potential risks or consequences, often in order to achieve something. (जोखिम उठाना या लापरवाह होना)

 
 
• **Example**: Despite the dangers of the stunt, he decided to **throw caution to the wind** and proceed with it anyway.
 
 
 
• **To take a big risk or be reckless** resonates with the essence of "**throw caution to the wind**," implying a willingness to face danger or act without worrying about the negative outcomes. (बड़ा जोखिम उठाना या लापरवाह होना)
 
 
• **Example**: She **threw caution to the wind** and invested all her savings into a new business venture.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 2**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To be indecisive or unsure about a decision** doesn't align with "throw caution to the wind," which suggests a definitive action taken regardless of risks.
 
• **To be overly cautious or hesitant** is the opposite of "throw caution to the wind," as the idiom implies a lack of caution.
 
• **To be too strict or rigid in following rules** is unrelated to the idea conveyed by "throw caution to the wind" and does not suggest taking risks or being reckless.
